item.description:
**Port forwarding.** Open a tunnel from the session's window (⌥⌘P), or save one to a host so it opens on connect. Both `-L` (a local port to a remote address) and `-D` (a SOCKS5 proxy) are there, and forwards ride the whole jump chain — the tunnel starts at the last hop, not the first. The window lists what is actually open, because a tunnel you cannot see is a tunnel you cannot trust.
**Files, next to the terminal.** The session window now carries a file pane above the terminal: the remote on top, this Mac below, either one switchable to any other connected machine. Dragging between the panes moves the file — including remote to remote, which relays through this Mac because SFTP has no server-side copy.
**Also new**
- Find in the scrollback (⌘F) - A colour per host, so production does not look like staging - A dot showing which sessions are actually up - Answer a `sudo` password prompt from your saved credentials, without the mouse - Sort the file list by name, size, or date; Return opens, Delete removes - A serial port remembers its own speed - Only one copy of the app runs, and there is a way back to the connect window - The sidebar shows whether you are on the trial or licensed
**Still missing** — folder-wise transfer, resuming an interrupted transfer, a transfer queue.
